correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the source definitions and uses its proved piecewise-linear formula for the follow-up frontier. On each interval between cumulative report masses, the AI information-cost curve is exactly the segment between adjacent breakpoint modes. This converts the perspective program to a finite linear program; scaling, an idle mode, and planar lower-hull geometry give the value formula, feasibility condition, and two-mode sparsity. The selective-value criterion follows from the monotonicity of Psi(s)/s for a concave Psi with Psi(0)=0. The outer reduction follows from the perspective of a convex piecewise-linear hull. Exact rational replay checks a nontrivial instance. No finite computation is used to justify the general theorem.

value.rationale: The source's lower bound is its benchmark for the asymptotically optimal policy, yet it is left as repeated convex optimization over pool size. The finite-hull identity exposes the exact information-cost geometry, proves that no more than two sensing modes are needed, gives a sharp condition for when selective escalation has value beyond pure-source mixing, and reduces the outer benchmark to finitely many explicit breakpoints and crossings. These are structural and computationally reusable facts tied to the paper's central cost-information question, not an arbitrary parameter slice or numerical recomputation.
